editorial.headline: Alternative-Market Derivatives Trading: Indonesia Open, Bali Clear
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers proprietary trading of eligible derivative contracts through an alternative trading-system mechanism, with full foreign ownership nationally and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
This activity is the proprietary buying and selling of derivative contracts—excluding futures contracts and sharia derivative contracts—through an alternative trading-system mechanism. The defining point is whose account is being served: the transactions are undertaken in the operator’s own name and for its own account. It is therefore a tightly framed trading activity, rather than a broad description of arranging transactions for others.

Registration is open across the full stated range of business scales: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. That breadth does not dilute the activity’s scope. A registrant should still be able to describe its operations in terms that remain faithful to proprietary trading of the specified contracts within an alternative trading system, rather than relying on a looser financial-services label.

Nationally, the activity is open to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. The record identifies Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 as the PMA source. In plain terms, there is no national foreign-equity cap below full ownership for this activity.

Bali’s position is also materially clearer than the usual concern around the province’s PMA moratorium. Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities for PMA registration on an island-wide, permanent basis. This activity is not blocked by that rule: at the Large scale, its OSS risk is Medium-High/High. The practical reading is not that Bali supplies a separate ownership figure or additional condition; it is that the moratorium does not prevent PMA registration for this activity. A founder considering Bali can therefore treat the activity as open nationally and not moratorium-blocked in Bali, while keeping the registration description disciplined around the proprietary derivative trading actually stated here.
editorial.pullQuote: Bali’s moratorium does not prevent PMA registration for this activity.
